diagnosis: Candidate/bad runs overrepeat operations without changing strategy or state.
expected_mechanism: The policy interrupts unproductive loops by requiring evidence of state change or a revised approach. Expected cost: lightweight state tracking and occasional early termination of a retry that might eventually succeed.
policy_text: Track recent operations and outcomes. If an operation is marked repeated, do not execute it again unless new evidence indicates the relevant state changed. Instead, change the strategy, obtain new information, or stop and report the blocker. Permit one justified retry for transient failures.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r '[.value, (.stack_frames[] | select(. == "result:repeated"))] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{if($1>0) bad+=$1; else good+=-$1} END {printf "bad=%d good=%d excess=%d ratio=%.2f\n",bad,good,bad-good,bad/good}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: Repeated-result operations total 1,485 on the candidate/bad side versus 224 on the base/good side: +1,261 excess and 6.63× as many.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r '.value' samples.jsonl | awk '{if($1>0) bad+=$1; else good+=-$1} END {printf "bad=%d good=%d\n",bad,good}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: All operations total 7,366 candidate/bad and 3,780 base/good. Thus repeated operations are 20.16% versus 5.93% of operations, a 3.40× higher share.
